# surefold

> Structured concurrency, resources, streams, actors and application wiring for
> Kotlin on the JDK's virtual threads, with no coroutines and no second effect
> system. Surefold's own `Fail` and `Either` are the error model throughout.

Facts worth having before anything else:

- Kotlin 2.4, JDK 25 or newer. Apache 2.0. On Maven Central as
  `io.github.matthewjones372:surefold` and sibling modules, all on one version.
- Releases are tagged `vX.Y.Z`. Between them, `X.Y.(Z+1)-SNAPSHOT` is
  published by hand, not on every push, to
  `https://central.sonatype.com/repository/maven-snapshots/`.
- Experimental: everything is tested, and the API can change in any `0.x`
  release. Pin an exact version.
- Each module brings at most the one external library or SDK it integrates,
  so depend only on the modules the code uses.
- Blocking is fine: every fork is a virtual thread. Do not reach for
  `suspend`, a dispatcher or a `CompletableFuture` where a surefold call exists.
- A service is a `Module` (a dependency graph) run by `SurefoldApp` and `runApp`.
  Resources are nodes the graph releases in reverse dependency order; a node's
  `close()` is the graph's job, not the class that holds it.
- Background work is a `Stream` started on the graph's `StreamBackend`
  (usually `Forks()`), not a scheduler or a thread of its own.
- Surefold's compiler plugin, applied with `id("io.github.matthewjones372.surefold.wiring")`,
  checks every graph as it compiles and warns where code hand-rolls what surefold
  ships: `SUREFOLD_RUN_NEVER_RETURNS_ON_SHUTDOWN`, `SUREFOLD_SCHEDULER_BY_HAND`,
  `SUREFOLD_SECRET_AS_STRING`, `SUREFOLD_SLEEP_IN_TEST`.

## Modules

- `surefold`: `scope`, `parZip`, `parMap`, `traverse`, `parTraverse`, `raceN`, `zipOrAccumulate`,
  `mapOrAccumulate`, `accumulate { }`, `resourceScope`, `Schedule`,
  `timeout`, `policy` (retry, circuit breaker, bulkhead, rate limiter),
  `SurefoldLocal`, `Clock`, `TestClock`, the log and metrics calls,
  `capturingLogs` and `capturingMetrics` for tests (`logger.unbound()` for
  what `main` reads), `await()` for a
  `CompletionStage` or `Future`, and `surefoldFuture { }` to hand one back.
- `surefold-replay`: `explore(runs) { }` runs a test's forks in a different seeded
  order each time and names the order that broke it; `replay(order) { }` runs that order again.
- `surefold-compiler`: a K2 checker for surefold's structure rules; a `Deferred`,
  `Channel` or `Scope` returned from a scope or kept in a property fails to compile.
  Applied by the Gradle plugin `io.github.matthewjones372.surefold.compiler`, in `surefold-app-gradle`.
- `surefold-pekko`: a Pekko dispatcher as the executor, and Pekko's Scala futures
  awaited from a fork.
- `surefold-cache`: `Cache(ttl, stale) { lookup }`, one lookup per key however many ask,
  a ttl read from each result so failures are kept too, and the last good value while the source fails.
- `surefold-stream`: `Stream<E, A>` as a description, with its failure in the type
  and no backend named.
- `surefold-stream-forks`: runs a `Stream` as a pull loop on one virtual thread;
  the usual backend.
- `surefold-stream-pekko`: runs a `Stream` on Pekko Streams, with the operators
  that take Pekko's types.
- `surefold-stream-actors`: runs a `Stream` on `surefold-actor`, an actor per run.
- `surefold-stream-test`: `TestStreams` and `TestClock`, every stage on the calling
  thread and time the test moves.
- `surefold-test`: `story` (Given, When, Then), `eventually(within)`.
- `surefold-junit`: a JUnit Platform engine; a `Suite` object's tests share one
  `Resource`, and Gradle and the IDE report them as Jupiter's.
- `surefold-junit-testkit`: `shouldHaveSucceeded`, `shouldHaveFailed`,
  `shouldHaveSkipped` and `failureOf` on a suite's run from `EngineTestKit`.
- `surefold-app`: an application as a value: `single`, `singleOf`, `closingOf`,
  `boundTo`, `overriding`, `subgraph`, probes, health, `testApp`, `SurefoldApp`,
  `awaitShutdown`.
- `surefold-app-typesafe`: a HOCON section as a node (`config`), every fault at
  once, `secret`, `Config.choosing`, `overridingConfig`, and where each setting
  came from (`origins`).
- `surefold-app-kotlinx`: a HOCON section read from its `@Serializable` class,
  `config<Settings>("section")` with no block.
- `surefold-app-liquibase`: a changelog as a node (`migrations`); readers take
  `surefold-app`'s `Migrated`.
- `surefold-app-flyway`: SQL scripts on Flyway as a node (`flyway`, `migrate`),
  on the graph's `DataSource` or one `connect` opens; readers take `Migrated`. The
  data modules' scripts by `SurefoldSchema`, and `fromLiquibase` to hand a
  database over from Liquibase once.
- `surefold-app-openfeature`: `openFeature { provider }`, the provider as a node; a
  `Client` node and `Flag.value()` read it, and readiness follows it.
- `surefold-app-openfeature-flagd`: `flagdFlags("flags")`, flags in flagd's schema
  as a HOCON section, evaluated in-process; brings gRPC and netty.
  `flagdFlags("flags", declared)` also checks every variant against its declared `Flag` at start.
- `surefold-actor-pekko`: `ref.ask(system, within) { replyTo -> … }`, asking a Pekko typed actor on the
  calling virtual thread; `receive { message -> when (message) { … } }`, `same()`, `stopped()` and
  `replyTo.answer(reply)` to write one; `context.pipeToSelf(::Loaded) { … }` runs a `Fail<E>` block on a virtual
  thread and sends its `Either` back as a message. No wiring graph.
- `surefold-app-pekko`: a Pekko typed actor as a node, keyed by its `ActorRef<T>`.
- `surefold-app-actor`: a `surefold-actor` scope as a node, and an actor as a node.
- `surefold-app-cluster`: a `surefold-cluster` membership as a node, joined as a HOCON
  section says.
- `surefold-app-gradle`: the Gradle plugin `io.github.matthewjones372.surefold.wiring`,
  which checks and draws every graph as it compiles, and `io.github.matthewjones372.surefold.compiler`,
  which applies `surefold-compiler`. It is on Maven Central,
  not the Plugin Portal, so `pluginManagement` needs `mavenCentral()`.
- `surefold-app-compiler`: the K2 checker behind it, which shows the same faults
  and warnings in the editor.
- `surefold-otel`: an OpenTelemetry `Context` that crosses a fork; on the classpath
  and nothing else.
- `surefold-jdbc-otel`: JDBC query tracing with a privacy boundary before OpenTelemetry observers.
- `surefold-openfeature`: `evaluatedFor(key, …) { }` and `useSurefold()`, so a flag read
  in a fork or an actor handler answers for the request that started it.
- `surefold-arrow`: Surefold's `Either`, `NonEmptyList` and `Fail` to and from
  Arrow's: `toArrow()`, `toSurefold()`, `surefold { }` and `arrow { }`.
- `surefold-assert`: checks for tests: `shouldBe`, `shouldBeRight` and `shouldBeLeft`
  for Surefold's `Either`, the string, collection and map matchers, and `withClue`; a
  failure names the test's line and its source.
- `surefold-slf4j`: surefold's log lines through SLF4J, annotations in the MDC; on the
  classpath and nothing else.
- `surefold-micrometer`: surefold's counters, gauges and timers on Micrometer's
  registry; on the classpath and nothing else.
- `surefold-kafka`: Kafka as a `Stream` on any backend: commit after the work,
  dead letters, transactions.
- `surefold-kafka-pekko`: `surefold-kafka` through Pekko's Kafka connector.
- `surefold-otel-test`: a tracer that keeps the spans it ends, for a service's own
  tests, without displacing `surefold-otel`'s context storage.
- `surefold-kafka-test`: a Kafka broker in the test JVM for a service's own tests,
  with helpers to send, read and see what a group committed.
- `surefold-actor`: an actor as a value, taking one turn per message on virtual
  threads, with no actor system.
- `surefold-actor-journal-jdbc`: `surefold-actor`'s journal and snapshots on JDBC.
- `surefold-jobs`: durable jobs on Postgres, enqueued in the caller's own transaction.
- `surefold-app-jobs`: a job worker as a `surefold-app` node, started after the migrations.
- `surefold-jobs-otel`: a span per run of a job, linked to the span that enqueued it.
- `surefold-files`: files on any S3-compatible store, with typed failures and an in-memory fake.
- `surefold-files-test`: MinIO in Testcontainers, a fresh bucket a call, for a service's own tests.
- `surefold-tenancy`: a tenant forks inherit, Postgres row-level security set for every transaction, and a system path through definer functions only.
- `surefold-tenancy-test`: checks that a service's tables keep two tenants apart, and that its system role reaches rows only through its functions.
- `surefold-tenancy-crypto`: a key per tenant under a KMS root key no backup holds, and an in-memory KMS.
- `surefold-tenancy-crypto-aws`: `AwsKms`, one AWS KMS key per tenant, found by alias.
- `surefold-jobs-tenancy`: each job's handler runs as the tenant its row names.
- `surefold-idempotency`: idempotency keys on Postgres, reserved atomically across instances, answers replayed.
- `surefold-ratelimit`: token buckets in memory or on Postgres, shared by every instance.
- `surefold-postgres-notify`: Postgres's `LISTEN` as a `Stream` of notifications in commit order, and `notify` to send.
- `surefold-cache-postgres`: `invalidating(cache) { payload -> key }`, a `Cache` told by `NOTIFY` that a row changed.
- `surefold-cache-tenancy`: `TenantCache`, a cache keyed by the bound tenant; `NoTenant` with none bound.
- `surefold-openfeature-postgres`: `PostgresFlags`, flags per tenant from a Postgres table: the tenant's row, then the null row.
- `surefold-cache-redis`: `RedisLayer`, a cache layer every instance shares on Redis, and `RedisInvalidations` over pub/sub.
- `surefold-auth`: sessions and credentials: Argon2id passwords, rotating sessions, magic links, TOTP, roles.
- `surefold-auth-oidc`: OpenID Connect sign-in on Nimbus: the code flow with PKCE, every ID token check.
- `surefold-actor-projection`: a journal as a `Stream`, for a read model that
  resumes where it left off.
- `surefold-actor-remote`: `surefold-actor` across nodes over one TCP connection per
  pair.
- `surefold-actor-remote-protobuf`: remote messages in Protobuf.
- `surefold-actor-remote-avro`: remote messages in Avro.
- `surefold-actor-remote-kotlinx`: remote messages from `@Serializable` classes.
- `surefold-cluster`: gossip membership, discovery and downing with no
  coordinator.
- `surefold-cluster-kubernetes`: cluster seeds from the pods API, and a Lease.
- `surefold-cluster-aws`: cluster seeds from Cloud Map or ECS, and a DynamoDB
  lease.

## What to reach for

| Want | Use |
|---|---|
| a value built once and shared | `singleOf(::Thing)` |
| a value that must be closed, and is `AutoCloseable` | `closingOf(::Thing)` |
| a value given back some other way | `singleOf(::Thing, Thing::stop)` |
| `main` | `object App : SurefoldApp<Root>()` and `exitProcess(runApp(App).code)`; `run` parks on `awaitShutdown()` by default |
| configuration | `config<Settings>("section") { … }` from `surefold-app-typesafe` |
| a password or token | `secret("password")`, never `string(…)` |
| a setting that picks a module | `choice<Settings, Provided> { … }` inside the graph, or `conf.choosing("section", read) { … }` |
| migrations | `migrations("db/changelog.sql")`, then take a `Migrated` |
| readiness | `.probe(name, timeout, attempts, interval) { … }` |
| background work on an interval | `Stream.tick(every)` started on the graph's `StreamBackend` |
| a call to something unreliable | `policy("…") { deadline(…); retry(…); attemptTimeout(…) }` |
| to stop calling something that is down | `guard(CircuitBreaker(…))` in a policy |
| a retry or backoff | `Schedule.exponential(…)`, `Schedule.spaced(…)` |
| a stream that restarts after a defect | `restartOnDefect(schedule)` |
| a log line, a counter, a timer | `logInfo`, `counter(…).increment()`, `timed(…) { … }` |
| a value from a future | `future.await()` |
| to hand back a future, or be called from coroutines | `surefoldFuture { … }`; a coroutine waits on it with kotlinx's `await` |
| a coroutine library's answer | `runBlocking { … }`, with no `fail` inside |
| a fake in a test | `.overriding(single<T> { … })` |
| a smaller test | `.subgraph<Root>()` and `testApp(module) { root -> … }` |
| a test that waits for something | `eventually(within) { … }`, never `Thread.sleep` |
| a test of something on a timer | `TestStreams` from `surefold-stream-test`, with `TestClock` |
| a test of a backoff | `clock.locally(fixedClock()) { … }`; not for `timeout`, which fires at once under it |

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/matthewjones372/lark/blob/main/README.md): what Surefold is, a first example, and where to go next.
- [Modules](https://github.com/matthewjones372/lark/blob/main/docs/modules.md): every module, what it adds, maturity, performance and limitations.
- [Core](https://github.com/matthewjones372/lark/blob/main/docs/core.md): forks, cancellation, errors, resources, schedules, timeouts, policies, context, Pekko dispatchers.
- [Applications](https://github.com/matthewjones372/lark/blob/main/docs/app.md): the graph, starting and stopping, probes, testing, the Gradle and compiler plugins.
- [Application cookbook](https://github.com/matthewjones372/lark/blob/main/docs/cookbook.md): one recipe per task, most compiled by a test.
- [Streams](https://github.com/matthewjones372/lark/blob/main/docs/stream.md), [Kafka](https://github.com/matthewjones372/lark/blob/main/docs/kafka.md), [Actors](https://github.com/matthewjones372/lark/blob/main/docs/actors.md), [Remoting and clusters](https://github.com/matthewjones372/lark/blob/main/docs/cluster.md), [Jobs](https://github.com/matthewjones372/lark/blob/main/docs/jobs.md), [Migrations on Flyway](https://github.com/matthewjones372/lark/blob/main/docs/flyway.md), [Files](https://github.com/matthewjones372/lark/blob/main/docs/files.md), [Tenancy](https://github.com/matthewjones372/lark/blob/main/docs/tenancy.md), [Idempotency and rate limits](https://github.com/matthewjones372/lark/blob/main/docs/http-stores.md), [Sign-in and sessions](https://github.com/matthewjones372/lark/blob/main/docs/auth.md).
- [Observability](https://github.com/matthewjones372/lark/blob/main/docs/observability.md) and [Testing](https://github.com/matthewjones372/lark/blob/main/docs/testing.md).
- [Feature flags](https://github.com/matthewjones372/lark/blob/main/docs/flags.md): `Flag`, `evaluatedFor`, `featureClient`.
